confidence_key.high: official source or multiple corroborating reports
confidence_key.low: one anecdotal report — a lead, not a fact
confidence_key.medium: single strong source or consistent forum consensus

legal_key.amber: Possible with conditions — call ahead, verify signage, or confidence is medium/low
legal_key.green: Overnight sleeping verified legal (permit/fees may apply)
legal_key.red: Banned — shown so the app explains WHY not to sleep here

_meta.rig: Tesla Model Y — stealth camping (passenger vehicle, NOT an RV)

camp_mode_rules: Camp Mode will NOT start below 20% battery — the car reserves the rest to drive out
Arrive ≥50% SoC (≥80% in deep cold); Sentry Mode OFF when camping
Set cabin 18–19°C + heated seats instead of 22°C; pre-condition while plugged in

features.name: Nootka St / Renfrew Park side streets
features.notes: Quiet residential side streets, no signage, iOverlander-verified. Vancouver takes no enforcement action just for living in a vehicle; the 10pm–6am ban applies only to vehicles >2.2m tall / >6.4m long — a Model Y is exempt. Enforcement is complaint-driven: arrive late, leave early.

features.name: Safeway — Caulfeild Village (West Van)
features.notes: Backup option: reported overnight OK with a manager call-ahead. Ask inside before settling in.

features.name: Supercharger — Richmond (Garden City Rd)
features.notes: 40-stall V3 — Canada's largest. Overnight play: charge off-peak before departure.

features.name: Supercharger — Burnaby (Bainbridge Ave)
features.notes: Cheapest off-peak rate in the area. Top up here before the drive to Crystal.

features.name: Crystal Mountain resort lots (B Lot)
features.notes: BANNED for passenger cars. Overnight is RV-only via Roverpass (~$55–65/night); a car is allowed only as a companion vehicle on a paid RV site. $100 boot threats documented (2022). Do not stealth here.

features.name: Silver Springs Sno-Park
features.notes: Best option: ~5 mi from resort on Crystal Mountain Blvd, plowed. Overnight camping explicitly legal in WA Sno-Parks with a permit — $25 one-day / $50 seasonal. Verify 'approved area' signage on arrival. Sleep here, drive up each morning.

features.name: Supercharger — Auburn (Outlet Collection)
features.notes: MUST-HIT before the climb — no fast charger exists in Enumclaw. Charge to ≥90%; budget ~2× rated miles for the 3,500-ft ascent in winter.

features.name: FLO Level 2 — at the resort
features.notes: Unverified FLO charger at the resort (33914 Crystal Mountain Blvd). Likely Level 2 — useful daytime top-up while skiing. Verify stall count in PlugShare first.

features.name: Big Sky Resort lots
features.notes: BANNED — 'Overnight parking and camping are not allowed at Big Sky Resort', no passenger-car carve-out. Active patrol; winter plow tows. Do not stealth here.

features.name: Big Sky Town Center
features.notes: BANNED — visitor overnight parking prohibited: ticket / boot / tow. Big Sky is unincorporated, so there are no public streets to fall back on.

features.name: Walmart — Bozeman
features.notes: ~45 mi north via US-191 (~1,500 ft descent). Multiple trip reports describe it as welcoming to overnighters. Call the manager, park far from the entrance.

features.name: MDT rest area — I-90 near Bozeman
features.notes: Montana explicitly allows 12-hour overnight parking; sleeping in the vehicle is permitted (official MDT policy). ~45 mi north of the resort. Pin is approximate — follow highway signage.

features.name: Supercharger — Big Sky Town Center
features.notes: 8 stalls, up to 150 kW, 24/7. ~2.5 mi from Mountain Village. Playbook: Supercharge by day, sleep in Bozeman (~45 mi north), drive back in the morning.

features.name: Steamboat Springs — town-wide winter ban
features.notes: BANNED — city winter ban reissued Oct 23, 2026: no overnight parking on streets/shoulders Nov 1–Apr 30, no overnight parking or camping at any public facility or lot. Ticketed/towed even when not snowing. Resort lots: no overnight.

features.name: Rabbit Ears Pass winter lots (Dumont Lake)
features.notes: Best option: ~20–25 mi SE on US-40 at ~9,400 ft. USFS describes Dumont lot as open year-round and popular with snowmobilers winter camping (~25 parties on winter Saturdays). US-40 is plowed year-round. Very cold, no facilities — a Model Y blends in.

features.name: Steamboat Springs KOA Holiday
features.notes: Paid fallback — open year-round. Use if the pass lots are unreachable in a storm.

features.name: Supercharger — Craig (Kum & Go)
features.notes: Nearest Supercharger to Steamboat — ~42 mi west on US-40. Charge high here on arrival/departure days. WARNING: Rawlins WY → Steamboat is ~130 mi with no Tesla fast charger — leave Rawlins near 100% in winter.

features.name: MagicDock — Kremmling
features.notes: ~30 mi SE of Steamboat. Pin is approximate — use the car's nav for the exact stall location.

features.name: ChargePoint DC fast — Kum & Go (in town)
features.notes: In-town top-up option — needs a CCS adapter. Pin is approximate; verify in the car's nav or PlugShare.

features.name: Gila Lot — overnight parking
features.notes: LIKELY PERMITTED: policy explicitly lists 'tents' and 'any overnight camping guests' — $30+tax/night Mon–Thu, $45+tax/night Fri–Sun & peak, 7-night max, no hookups, portable toilets. A Model Y paying the rate is very likely fine, but passenger cars are never named — call 800-776-1111 to confirm a car-only booking. Closest legal sleep to the lifts.

features.name: Walmart — Taos
features.notes: Backup: a 2023 report says the manager approved overnights. Call 575-758-1136 night-of. Town of Taos bans overnight parking at all town facilities.

features.name: TSV DC fast chargers
features.notes: 8 public DC fast ports at the resort itself. Evening top-up, then move to the Gila Lot — don't sit on a plug overnight (idle fees).

features.name: TSV Level 2 chargers
features.notes: 14 public Level 2 ports at the resort. Good for a slow top-up while skiing.

features.name: Supercharger — Raton NM
features.notes: Last fast charger on approach — ~75 mi out via US-64. Charge high here (~2,000 ft climb on NM-150 in the cold).

features.name: Snowbird resort lots
features.notes: BANNED — lodge-guest permit only. Alta's marshal tows non-permitted cars to the valley (>$800). Do not stealth up-canyon.

features.name: Cottonwood Canyon roadsides
features.notes: BANNED — watershed order: sleeping in a vehicle prohibited within ½ mile of any road in the Cottonwood Canyons, year-round. No roadside parking 12am–7am. During Interlodge, being in a vehicle is a Class B misdemeanor. Everything must be down-canyon in the Salt Lake Valley.

features.name: Cabela's — Lehi
features.notes: ~25–30 min south of the canyon mouth. Signs say no overnight in the upper lot, but the customer-service desk has OK'd it — ask on arrival.

features.name: SLC Valley side streets (Cottonwood Heights)
features.notes: Quiet suburban streets down-canyon. Winter street bans vary by city — verify signage block by block. Companion fact: UTA Ski Bus Route 994 (Sandy→Snowbird) is FREE with an Ikon Pass — park down-canyon, bus up, skip the traction-law gamble.

features.name: Supercharger — Midvale
features.notes: Brackets the canyon mouth with Draper and South Jordan — all ~15–25 min from Snowbird base. Pattern: evening Supercharge → sleep down-canyon on battery → bus or drive up in the morning.

features.name: Supercharger — Draper
features.notes: ~15–25 min from Snowbird base. Snowbird's own garage chargers are lodge-guest-only with a 4-hour move rule — not usable.

features.name: Supercharger — South Jordan
features.notes: ~15–25 min from Snowbird base.
